newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China plans big nuclear power plant in Guangdong.
newsitem.headline: China plans big nuclear power plant in Guangdong.

text.p: China is planning to build what it said would be its biggest nuclear plant, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Tuesday.
The Yangjiang Nuclear Power Plant, 250 km southwest of Hong Kong, would be built in three phases.
It would have six generators with a capacity of 1,000 megawatts each and the first phase of construction was expected to cost US$3.5 billion, the newspaper said.
Experts are conducting feasibility studies in the waters near the plant site in southwestern Guangdong. It did not give a timetable for the project or any other details.
China currently has two commercial nuclear power plants -- Daya Bay Nuclear Power Plant in Shenzhen city bordering Hong Kong, and Qinshan Nuclear Power Plant in eastern Zhejiang province.
